text_original:
Hey kiddo, Handsome Jack here... and I just played Street Fighter 6, and honestly? The actual game is fantastic. Great combat, great characters, gorgeous visuals, tons of content, and enough ways to beat another human being unconscious that I'm starting to think this is less of a fighting game and more of a very elaborate employee dispute resolution system.

The fighting feels fantastic. Every punch feels good, every combo feels satisfying, and when you land a perfect counter and absolutely demolish someone, you feel like a tactical genius.

Then I opened the store.

Oh.

OH, KIDDO.

So you're telling me characters that were already available in previous Street Fighter games are now something I have to BUY AGAIN?

Interesting.

Very interesting.

At Hyperion, when an employee already exists, we don't sell them back to the customer every time they walk into the building.

Well, actually, we probably would.

But I'm evil.

What's your excuse?

You already bought Ryu.

You've had Ryu.

You've known Ryu.

Ryu has been punching people since before some of these monetization systems were invented.

And now you're telling me I need to purchase him again?

THE MAN HASN'T EVEN CHANGED HIS SHIRT.

And then you've got costumes, premium currency, battle passes, DLC characters, special editions, cosmetic nonsense...

Kiddo, I came here to punch people.

Why am I negotiating with a virtual currency?

The worst part is that the base game is genuinely excellent. That's what makes it so frustrating. The developers clearly know how to make an incredible fighting game. The gameplay is polished, the roster is fun, the World Tour mode is surprisingly entertaining, and the overall presentation is fantastic.

Then someone from Accounting walks into the room and says:

“Hey, what if we charged them for that?”

GET OUT.

Nobody invited Accounting.

So yeah, the fighting gets a 9/10.

The game gets dragged down by the monetization.

5/10 overall.

Fantastic fighting game.

Terrible relationship with my wallet.

I'd give it a 6, but every time I see a character I remember already owning somewhere else, my score drops another point.

At this rate, by Street Fighter 7 I'll be paying $4.99 to unlock the start button.

And honestly?

I wouldn't put it past them.

Hyperion approves of the business model.

Unfortunately, I also approve of good customer service.

So I'm conflicted.

text_original: I've played a couple of fighting games in the past, but only for a couple hours or so each - they always seemed really obtuse and hard to get into. Also really dry. SF6 has a great single player story mode that's fun and teaches you a lot of concepts in the game at a steady pace, as well as normal arcade/story modes for each character which is really cool. The characters are all really fun to play, and different from each other. I'm having a lot of fun learning and it's really rewarding to improve over time. I haven't played much ranked yet, but all the other modes in the game have been really engaging. This is a great first fighting game to get into if you're interested in the genre (or Street Fighter specifically) and haven't been able to break through.

text_original:
Despite the hate you'd find surrounding the game, it's really well done. It's like the first fighting game I've ever played outside of the normal Mortal Kombat/Tekken mash with cousins as a kid. I bought the game on December 2025 and have been hooked ever since.

I forced myself onto Classic and now I don't really regret it, but it was a very rough start. I spent a few weeks in rookie (the lowest rank in the game), eating shit every single game, losing to literally the worst players in the game. The moment the inputs clicked, the game made sense, and the few guide videos I watched made sense I started climbing, and I'm now grateful I didn't start with Modern, but that's just how I played the game. 

If you're scared from this beginning period of eating shit over and over and having your ego dismantled then Modern is YOUR path. The difference between the two isn't really present unless in really high levels and even there you can find Modern players competing and reaching high levels. So don't overthink it really.

SF6 is a treasure, and I hope Capcom doesn't do any rash changes when the game's really polished and fun. If you're on the fence about buying the game then do yourself a favor and snag it. If you're still hesitant and unsure then do yourself even more of a favor and play Modern. Trust me Classic is only for the people who are ready to have their ego dismantled and won't get discouraged by a few weeks of getting rekt left, right, and center.

Please, do us a favor, and make the FGC bigger. Buy this game, and talk to your friend group and rope them into this too #notsponsored. The only bad thing about SF6 and the FGC in general is the obvious lower numbers of players, don't get me wrong, SF6 is thriving at the timing of this review's release, but it is nowhere near the level the game deserves. Drop whatever MOBA, FPS, Gacha, or Battle Royale game you've been grinding and hop onto Fighting Games, where the only person to blame for your loss is you and the balance team, say goodbye to those godawful teammates, trolls, and toxic players. It's you and your teabagger opponent, nothing more, nothing less.

text_original:
Extremely Frustrating User Experience
Worst User Interface in 20 Years on Steam: The menus are a convoluted, anti-consumer nightmare. Basic options are deeply buried, and somehow failed to put a straightforward "Quit to Desktop" option on the main title screen.

Aggressive Online Account Shoveling: The game relentlessly forces you to create and log into an external "Capcom ID" account every single time you boot it up. Even if you just want to play offline against bots, it constantly stops you with corporate logins.

Forced Onboarding and No Freedom: It completely disregards player control. It traps you inside specific modes and aggressively demands you use a character creator before you can back out or just play a traditional match.

Terrible Visual Execution: The graphic interface is completely obscured and illegible right out of the gate. On top of that, the artistic direction pushes jarring, visually mismatched character aesthetics that feel heavily driven by a corporate checklist rather than good taste.

Zero Respect for the Classic Fighting Experience: If you just want to log in, select a traditional roster character, pick a tier, and fight against CPU bots (like Mortal Kombat), this game forces you to jump through a dozen frustrating, unnecessary social-hub hoops first.

text_original:
The Good 
-Casual Friendly with easy controls for people to pick up and play
-Tons of players
-A decent roster size at this point
-Easy to swap characters if your in a rough drought 
-Game runs well and has the best netcode
-Animations look great

The Bad
-Modern controls hurts the balance and design of the game which leaves characters in awkward states 
-Game does no changes because they are scared to do antyhing
-Raw drive rush, drive rush fireball, throw loops,  Brainless offense needs to be removed/toned down 
-Defensive mechanics do not exist - all the defense mechanics are directly used for generating offense - drive reversal is unreliable and if your playing a character with no dp or reversal level 1.....  your going to hate your life.
-People can rage quit at the end of a match in masters to avoid giving you points even though the games over
-People will turn on the lag switch randomly with no bans
-People are actually caught for cheats and all they get is a rank reset
-Nobody plays footsies in this game because of all the neutral skip garbage slop
-Character balance on the surface level seems very good until you realize its trash
-Balance changes like doubling down on throw loops, ryu apparently having issues generating offense and somehow zangief players being confused at when russian suplex will come out .....? who wrote these patch notes - clearly someone with 0 iq.
-S4 pass is TERRIBLE outside tifa
-Yasmine is by far the worst character i've ever seen in a fighting game period.

You can blame the balance team, you can blame the planning team - but really if you ask players how they feel about the game state that play ranked..... they will tell you its stale and boring and this is NAKAYAMAS fault, terrible director and should be fired immediately - i do not sympathize with developers that ask for 80 dollar base game -> 40 CAD season passes. Charging this much, you better deliver  or prepare to be critiqued.

text_original: Game is highly addictive, even when you're bad at it. I, for one, am horrible at fighting games, and every time I lose I feel really bad and have the urge to self harm. Thanks to this game my wrists have lots of new scars, and people around me have been telling me to quit and find help. Frankly, I completely agree with them, and every time I boot up this game, my hands start shaking. I've probably uninstalled this game and reinstalled like ten times already. However, I made a lot of friends playing this game, and getting my ass kicked by them is a bit better than by strangers online. It's a fun game in the hands of someone who knows what they're doing, and it needs a lot of time, energy and patience. I hope y'all have fun, enjoy life, and picks lots of fights in lots of streets!

text_original:
Long time Street Fighter player since release in my childhood. I'm soo nostalgic for this game. I mainly love to play against my son who can now beat me.. which makes me soo proud.

Over the years SF has had it's ups and downs. Up with the releases through SF Alpha, down with SFIII, up again with SF4,5.  But with SF6, Capcom has turned SF into a confusing mess of ideas that fail to inspire. 
I still play from time to time mainly because I feel SF6 has one of the best versions of Dhalsim, my main man! 
For the most part the OG characters, Ryu, Ken, Guile, E.Honda, Chun-li, Zangief etc. are faithful, progressed in meaningful ways and are very fun to play still.
The new characters are unbelievable pairings of nationalities+fighting styles and for the most part have cringey unlikable personalities.

There's just too much of one mood throughout the game. The constant pumping of vocals filled music of any genre gets old really fast, especially with rap. Musical tastes vary too much from one person/culture/region to another to make one selection so prominent. It would be better to use ambient music without vocals in the intros and character selection screens. Then once the character stages are selected, play the corresponding regional ambient music with limited vocals. Capcom's take on American culture, specifically the inner-city vibe is not endearing, not necessarily offensive, just so off that I hate to see how much of it was infused into the theme of this release. They really need to tone it down. In my opinion the American and non-American audience alike would probably be more receptive to other cultural influences. 

Overall, SF4, SF5 way better than SF6

Oh yeah... pricing is too dang high. I've already spent too much on the base game. Not gonna spend more than $5 per new character.

text_original: I think this is the best modern introductory fighting game along with Gran Blue Versus: Rising. It has the newer mechanics that the original Street Fighter games don't have, like Drive Rush, Impact, etc., but it is not as overwhelming as your anime fighters with their overloaded mechanics, even though the ceiling is still extremely high. I just like how it has a fair entry point, where you will still get your ass kicked by those who understand the game more efficiently. It feels perfectly made, in terms of presentation, music, and the attention catching UI choices like with your victories, etc. I remember when I got into the game during the beta, I realized quickly that it would become a top fighting game because of its style and the appeal it could have for new players needing to intrigue them. I think the hub is also a fun thing that many people seem to enjoy for socializing. I would recommend this for sure, even if you know nothing about the genre.
